strategy.summary: Trade the INTRADAY spread between ES and RTY, flat by the close every day (no overnight holds). Each leg is measured from that day's open, so the spread starts at 0 each session; when ES runs ahead of or behind β × RTY by an unusual amount, bet on the gap closing before the close. β comes from Ning & Lee (Purdue Statistics, 2024): the ratio whose spread reverts fastest (the empirical mean-reversion time, EMRT), fit monthly on these intraday spreads. The OLS slope and 1:1 run alongside as controls. Designed after v1, whose flat-at-close versions all failed because its multi-day spread rarely reverted within the day.
strategy.formula: spread = (ES − today's ES open) ÷ open − β × (RTY − today's RTY open) ÷ open; β = argmin EMRT

rules.label: Hedge
rules.text: At each month start, fit β on the previous 1, 3 or 6 months only. EMRT: mark every swing of at least C × the spread's sd (an 'important extremum'), time how long each takes to get back to the mean within the same session (a swing still open at the close counts until the close), and pick the β from 0.20 to 3.00 with the shortest average (C = 1.5 or 2.0), as long as the spread's variance is at most 2× the OLS spread's. Controls: OLS slope; β = 1.

rules.label: Enter
rules.text: z = the spread against the formation window's mean and sd, or by time of day: against the same bar of the last 20 or 60 sessions. A fresh cross below −entry buys the spread (long ES, short β × RTY); above +entry sells it. Both legs fill at the next bar's open. Optionally no entries in the first 30 minutes; none in the last 30; a signal while a position is open is dropped.

rules.label: Exit
rules.text: Close when z gets back to 0 (at mean) or half-way to it; optional stop once z runs a further 1.5 past the entry level; optional time stop after 3 × the spread's EMRT. Anything still open is closed at the session's last close: never held overnight.

rules.label: Size
rules.text: Both / long spread / short spread; one position at a time. Whole ES and RTY contracts, the two legs' full contract value together no more than the account (no leverage), starting from $10,000,000 so the ratio is carried by tens of contracts.

strategy.length_note: Formation is in months; time-of-day windows are in sessions; EMRT and time stops are in bars.

funnel.name: Start
funnel.why: All 13,824 versions backtested once on 2018–2022 data.

funnel.name: 1 · Integrity
funnel.why: Per-trade checks on every version: the spread's z was recomputed by a separate route, each hedge was fit only on months before the trade, each entry was a fresh cross on an allowed side, no qualifying signal was skipped while flat, both legs filled at the next open no better than the market, exits fired at the first bar a rule did, and P&L, roll costs and sizing add up. Plus 40 random versions re-run on cut-off data. 0 failed.

funnel.name: 2 · Enough trades
funnel.why: Needs ≥100 completed trades and ≥10 a year in ≥4 of the 5 years. Removed 4,145 (1,557 on 5min, 2,588 on 15min).

funnel.name: 3 · Profit
funnel.why: Needs a net profit, Sharpe ≥ 0.75 and drawdown no worse than 30%. Removed 9,600 (5,280 on 5min, 4,320 on 15min); 7,966 of them lost money.

funnel.name: 4 · Stable settings
funnel.why: Each setting is nudged one at a time, down and up: the formation window and a rolling z window by ±20% (rounded, at least one month / bar), the entry |z| by ±0.25, a stop by ±0.25 z, an EMRT hedge's C by ±0.25 and a time stop by ±0.5 × EMRT ("none" has nothing to nudge). At least 70% of the nudged versions must be profitable, with median Sharpe ≥ 0.5. Removed 2.

funnel.name: 6 · Remove duplicates
funnel.why: Versions whose monthly returns correlate ≥ 0.8 form a group; the best 2 of each go on (a group of one keeps its one). 59 versions formed 5 groups; 10 of the 10 picks are distinct backtests.

funnel.name: 8 · Validation
funnel.why: Frozen finalists run once on unseen data: needs net > 0, Sharpe ≥ 0.3, drawdown no worse than 30% and ≥40 trades.

assumptions: Data: Databento CME continuous front month (ES.v.0 and RTY.v.0), 1-minute bars aggregated to 5 minutes and 15 minutes and joined on bar time (a bar missing in either leg is dropped from both). Rolls are back-adjusted per leg; the spread uses only real point moves scaled by real prices.
Day session only: NYSE regular session 09:30-16:00 NY for both legs, on NYSE trading days.
Costs on EACH leg: 1 tick slippage per side (stops too) and $2.50 commission per contract per side; holding over a roll costs that leg a round turn.
Every position is closed at the session's last close, so nothing is held overnight and no trade crosses a contract roll (prop-firm compatible).

Unlevered across both legs, so returns are small next to a single-market strategy; a market-neutral book would normally run levered. Sharpe doesn't depend on that choice; return and drawdown scale with it.
The paper tested daily stock pairs with a reinforcement-learning trader. Here a plain z band trades a session-anchored intraday spread, so the whole grid is an extrapolation of the paper.
Decisions use both legs' bar closes and fill at the next bar's open on both legs.
Sharpe uses daily mark-to-market returns (√252) of both legs, with idle cash earning 0%. Time in market is the share of bars with an open position.
Benchmark row: holding ES alone, for scale; the spread is roughly market-neutral and not trying to beat it.
Other strategy families were already selected on these legs' 2023–2024 data, so 2023–2024 is not untouched; only the 2025+ holdout is (and single-market picks were already scored on it).
Holdout (2025 onward) has not been run. It is a one-time final test and needs an explicit go-ahead.
